name: Manage daily cash and release payments (equipment finance company)
summary: Every business day the treasury and cash analyst works out how much cash the company has and needs, and pays the dealers and brokers whose deals were funded. The analyst reconciles the bank balances and the previous day's collections, splits collections between the bank warehouse line and the three conduit pools, checks the funding team's approved payables, builds the cash position and prepares any draw, repayment or rollover on the bank line; the treasurer approves the position and releases the payment file in the bank portal. The work is spreadsheet-based and runs against fixed deadlines: bank cut-offs for same-day EFT, notice periods for bank line advances and conduit remittance dates. Questioned payables, late funding approvals, rejected payments and an absent approver push payments to an afternoon run or the next day.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian equipment lessor with 340 staff, funding about 1,400 contracts a month on a syndicated bank warehouse line and refinancing them through three bank-sponsored ABCP conduits, with a six-person treasury team.
baseline.notes: Single legal entity with Canadian dollar accounts at one clearing bank; cash positioning in spreadsheets from bank portal downloads, payables approved in the lease system and released through the bank's cash management portal.

trigger: The bank's prior-day reports become available at the start of a business day, with approved payables waiting in the treasury queue and the previous day's collections balanced by cash application.
end_state: The day's vendor payments and broker commissions are released and confirmed, the bank line is drawn, repaid or rolled as needed, conduit remittances due are made, and the day's treasury entries are posted to the ledger.

volume.seasonality: One case per business day. Funding volumes peak at month end and quarter end, when dealers push deliveries, and around conduit settlement dates; 2020 saw fewer fundings and more payment deferrals.

evidence.note: Business days per month; matches the organisation file's process map.

Organisation file loaded cost (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Job Bank median $43.27 (2023-2024) times 0.9 times 1.35 gives about $53; the organisation file's $48 mode sits slightly below. About one of the two analysts spends most of each day on positioning and payment release; the other covers borrowing base, covenant reporting and back-up.
Organisation file loaded cost (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Reviews the position and releases payments for about 30 to 60 minutes a day.
Organisation file loaded cost (2019-2022 wage times 1.35). Back-up approver for large wires and when the treasurer is away.

systems.name: Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Data warehouse and business intelligence reports

steps.name: Bank prior-day reports load overnight
steps.description: Overnight the clearing bank publishes prior-day balance and transaction reports for every account and the settlement and return files for the debits and payments of the previous day, and the lease system finishes its nightly posting of the previous day's cash application.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Gathering balances from bank portals is the first step of setting the cash position; the overnight timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Download prior-day balances and activity
steps.description: When the treasury and cash analyst starts the day, they log in to the bank cash management portal, download the prior-day balance and transaction reports for the operating, lockbox, debit collection, payroll, conduit collection and reserve accounts, and paste them into the daily cash position workbook.

error.defect_description: A balance pasted against the wrong account or a stale report used.

evidence.note: Positioning from bank portal data in spreadsheets is common practice; minutes are an author estimate. Wait runs from the reports being available (about 6:30 a.m.) to the analyst starting (about 7:30 to 8:00 a.m.).

steps.name: Check debit settlement and returned items
steps.description: The analyst compares the settlement credit for the pre-authorised debit file due yesterday with the file total that billing released, notes the total of returned debits from the bank's return report, and checks that the lockbox and EFT deposits match what cash application expects.

error.defect_description: A short settlement or a large return batch is not noticed.

evidence.note: Typical check for a lessor where about 85% of customers pay by pre-authorised debit (organisation file); minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile yesterday's forecast to actual balances
steps.description: The analyst compares yesterday's expected closing position with the actual bank balances, line by line: debits settled, vendor payments cleared, bank line advances, conduit proceeds and bank fees, and lists any difference above the tolerance for research.

error.defect_description: A difference is explained away without proof and carries forward.

next.condition: an unexplained item, such as an unknown wire or a missing settlement

evidence.note: Reconciling bank activity and comparing actuals with forecast are described practices; the 15% rate of unexplained items is an author estimate.

steps.name: Research an unexplained bank item
steps.description: The analyst looks up the item in the bank portal detail, asks cash application whether a large customer payment or payout arrived, asks the securitisation analyst about conduit settlements, or calls the bank's cash management service about an unknown debit, fee or a payment that did not settle.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: item explained or logged as an open query

evidence.note: Analysts follow up discrepancies and decide whether the error is the bank's or internal; minutes and wait are author estimates.

steps.name: Pull collections by pool from cash application
steps.description: The analyst opens the balanced daily cash report that cash application closes each evening and the data warehouse report of collections by contract and pool, and splits yesterday's collections between contracts on the bank warehouse line, the balance sheet and each of the three conduit pools.

error.defect_description: A payout on a sold contract is left in the warehouse bucket.

evidence.note: Matches the hand-off in the apply-customer-payments workflow (step s20); the wait covers mornings when the cash report is late.

steps.name: Track conduit collections and remittances due
steps.description: The analyst adds the day's collections on each conduit pool to the collections tracker, checks the amount held against what each servicing agreement allows the company to keep before the next settlement date, and flags any remittance or reserve top-up that falls due.

error.defect_description: A remittance due date is missed, which can breach the servicing agreement.

control.basis: Conduit servicing agreements: collections on sold contracts are held for the conduit and remitted on schedule, with daily monitoring where commingling is allowed (DBRS commingling criteria)

next.condition: a conduit settlement date or settlement statement received

evidence.note: Rating criteria require daily monitoring when a servicer commingles collections and remittance within three business days otherwise; the exact terms of this lessor's facilities are not public.

steps.name: Confirm conduit settlement figures and plan the paydown
steps.description: On a conduit settlement date the analyst takes the settlement statement from the securitisation analyst, checks the purchase price, fees and reserve deposit against the conduit portal, and plans how much of the proceeds repays the bank warehouse line and how much funds the reserve account.

error.defect_description: Fees or reserve misread so the paydown is overstated.

evidence.note: Matches the hand-off in the sell-securitisation-pools workflow (step s20); three conduits each settle once a month, about 3 of 22 business days.

steps.name: Download the vendor and broker payment queue
steps.description: The analyst runs the lease system report of approved vendor payables and broker commissions placed in the treasury payment queue by the funding team since the last run, with counts, totals and same-day requests from dealers, and copies the totals into the cash position.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Matches the audit-and-fund-contracts workflow (step s21), where funding staff place approved payables in the treasury queue and never release cash; about 64 fundings and 20 broker commissions a business day from the organisation file's 1,400 fundings a month.

steps.name: Check the queue for approvals, duplicates and banking changes
steps.description: The analyst checks that every payable shows the required second approval in the lease system, sorts by vendor and amount to spot duplicates of earlier payments, looks for vendors whose banking changed in the last few days and checks that large items carry the manager's approval.

error.defect_description: A duplicate payable or a fraudulent banking change is not spotted.

control.basis: Payment release policy: treasury independently checks approvals, duplicates and recent banking changes before releasing funds (fraud prevention for payments)

evidence.note: Fraud prevention on payments is a core analyst task and business email compromise targeted 76% of organisations in 2020; the checks and the 10% query rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Hold questioned payables and query the funding team
steps.description: The analyst removes the questioned payables from today's release and emails the funding supervisor with the reason: a missing approval, a possible duplicate or banking that changed after a recent email. Held items return to the queue once funding confirms or corrects them.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Typical exception handling; the funding team's answer usually arrives in time for the afternoon run.

steps.name: Build the cash position and short-term forecast
steps.description: In the workbook the analyst sets the opening available balance, adds expected receipts (today's debit settlement, lockbox and EFT receipts, conduit proceeds) and subtracts today's outflows (vendor payments, broker commissions, interest, payroll or supplier runs, conduit remittances and tax remittances), compares the result with the minimum balance and works out the funding gap or surplus.

error.defect_description: A known outflow such as a tax remittance or payroll funding is left out.

evidence.note: Steps of setting the position are described by AFP; the daily cash position is the largest spreadsheet task in Kyriba's survey; minutes are an author estimate for a single-entity lessor.

steps.name: Treasurer reviews the position and decides on the bank line
steps.description: The treasurer reviews the position, the payment total and the remaining availability on the bank line, questions unusual items, and decides whether to draw on the line, repay it with surplus or conduit proceeds, roll a maturing bankers' acceptance, or leave it unchanged.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Treasury policy: daily position and funding decisions approved by the treasurer

next.condition: no change to the bank line

evidence.note: A shortfall is met by drawing on a revolving facility and a surplus can reduce debt; the 50% share of days with a bank line transaction is an author estimate for a lessor funding about $3.5 million of equipment a day and repaying the line from three monthly conduit sales.

steps.name: Check availability under the borrowing base
steps.description: The analyst compares the outstanding advances plus the proposed draw with the facility limit and the availability in the latest borrowing base certificate, adjusted for contracts sold to conduits since then, so the draw does not exceed eligible receivables.

error.defect_description: Availability overstated because sold contracts were not removed.

control.basis: Credit agreement: advances limited to the lesser of the commitment and the borrowing base

next.condition: availability short; treasurer must re-decide, for example defer payments

evidence.note: Borrowing base limits are standard in warehouse facilities (organisation file process report-credit-facility-covenants); the 4% shortfall rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the drawdown, repayment or rollover notice
steps.description: The analyst fills in the agent bank's notice template with the amount, date and type of advance (prime rate loan or bankers' acceptance and its term), checks the minimum amounts and the notice deadline, and prepares it for an authorised signatory.

error.defect_description: Wrong date, type or amount on the notice.

evidence.note: Sample Canadian facility: prime loans need notice by 9:00 a.m. one business day before, in multiples of Cdn$100,000; bankers' acceptances three business days before with Cdn$1,000,000 minimum. This lessor's facility terms are not public.

steps.name: Treasurer signs and sends the notice to the agent bank
steps.description: The treasurer checks the notice against the decision, signs it as an authorised officer and emails or uploads it to the agent bank before the deadline; a late notice moves the advance to the next business day.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Credit agreement: borrowing notices signed by an authorised officer and delivered by the agent's deadline

evidence.note: Notice deadlines from a sample Canadian facility; who signs is an author estimate.

steps.name: Agent bank funds or applies the advance
steps.description: The agent bank confirms the notice, credits a prime rate advance to the operating account or applies a repayment, or schedules a bankers' acceptance issue for its drawdown date. The analyst carries on with the payment file while this happens.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Timing depends on the notice period; the wait shown is the part that holds up the day's work, since most notices are given a day ahead.

steps.name: Build the EFT payment file and any wires
steps.description: The analyst releases the cleared payables from the lease system into a payment file in the bank's format, uploads it to the bank portal, keys wires for large mid-ticket fundings or same-day dealer requests, and checks the file count and total against the cleared list before submitting it for approval.

error.defect_description: A payable left out or a file uploaded twice.

next.condition: internal transfers or conduit remittances due

evidence.note: File upload, validation and approval workflow described in bank guides; the file must reach the bank by the 2:15 p.m. ET cut-off for same-day funds at direct clearers.

steps.name: Prepare internal transfers and conduit remittances
steps.description: The analyst keys the account transfers the position needs: moving debit and lockbox collections to the operating account, funding the payroll account, remitting collections or a reserve top-up to a conduit's collection account, and paying a sales tax remittance on its due date.

error.defect_description: A transfer keyed to the wrong account or amount.

control.basis: Conduit servicing agreements: remit collections and reserve amounts when due

evidence.note: Executing transfers is the last positioning step; conduit remittance rules come from rating criteria; frequency of about one day in three is an author estimate.

steps.name: Treasurer approves and releases payments in the bank portal
steps.description: The treasurer logs in to the bank portal with a security token, compares the pending file, wires and transfers with the cleared payment list and the cash position, and approves them; the analyst who created them cannot approve them. Wires above the treasurer's limit go to the chief financial officer.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Bank dual authorization: payments created by one user must be authorised by a different user; company signing authority limits

next.condition: wire above the treasurer's limit or treasurer away
returned: totals do not agree or an item must come out

evidence.note: Separate rights to create and authorise payments are standard in Canadian business banking; limits and the 8% referral rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Chief financial officer approves a large wire or covers for the treasurer
steps.description: The chief financial officer reviews a large wire against its funding approval, or the whole release when the treasurer is away, and approves it in the bank portal with their own token.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company signing authority policy and bank dual authorization

evidence.note: Typical back-up approval in a small treasury team; the threshold is not public.

steps.name: Bank validates the file and sends payments at the exchange
steps.description: The bank validates the approved file within minutes and returns an acknowledgement, then sends the EFT credits to the clearing exchange at the next cut-off, with funds reaching direct-clearing banks the same evening and some smaller institutions later; wires settle in real time.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Cut-offs at 5:00 a.m., 2:15 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. ET. The wait shown is to the bank's acknowledgement; the exchange itself runs while the analyst carries on.

steps.name: Check the bank acknowledgement and rejects
steps.description: The analyst checks the bank's acknowledgement that the file was accepted with the right count and total and reviews the rejects report for credits refused because of an invalid transit or account number.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: a payment or the file rejected

evidence.note: Originators review the returns and rejects report every business day; the 5% reject rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Correct a rejected payment with the funding team
steps.description: The analyst tells the funding specialist which vendor payment was rejected and why; funding confirms the correct banking with the vendor by call-back, the vendor master is fixed by someone who does not fund deals, and the analyst re-keys the payment for release.

error.defect_description: Banking changed on an unverified request.

evidence.note: Mirrors the vendor call-back and set-up controls in the audit-and-fund-contracts workflow (steps s10 and s11); waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Mark payments paid and send the payment report to funding
steps.description: The analyst marks the released payables as paid in the lease system with the payment date and file reference and posts the payment report where the funding team picks it up to send funding notices to dealers and brokers.
outputs: paid status in the lease system

error.defect_description: A payable marked paid that was held, or the reverse.

next.condition: payables approved after the morning cut-off go in an afternoon run

evidence.note: Matches the audit-and-fund-contracts workflow (step s22), where the specialist checks the payment report after treasury's EFT run; the 20% share of days with a second run is an author estimate.

steps.name: Record the day's treasury entries in the ledger
steps.description: Late in the day the analyst prepares the journal for bank line advances and repayments, bankers' acceptance discounts, interest and standby fees, conduit proceeds and reserve deposits, internal transfers and bank fees, attaches the bank confirmations and posts it to the ledger for the accounting team.

error.defect_description: An advance or fee posted to the wrong account or period.

evidence.note: Typical split in which treasury records financing entries and accounting reconciles them at month end (close-the-month workflow, step s08); minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Update the rolling cash forecast and share it
steps.description: Once a week the analyst rolls the 13-week cash forecast forward with actuals, updates expected fundings from the pipeline and conduit sale dates, explains large variances, and sends it to the treasurer, the chief financial officer and the securitisation analysts for pool sizing.
inputs: daily cash positions for the week

error.defect_description: Pipeline or conduit timing assumptions are stale.

evidence.note: Rolling 13-week forecasts updated weekly with bank actuals are described practice; the cash forecast feeds the sell-securitisation-pools workflow (step s02).

exceptions.name: Questioned payable held
exceptions.description: Treasury finds a payable without its second approval, a possible duplicate or banking that changed recently and holds it until funding confirms; it usually goes in the afternoon run.

exceptions.name: Bank line draw, repayment or rollover
exceptions.description: The position shows a gap or a surplus, or a bankers' acceptance matures, so the analyst checks borrowing base availability and the treasurer signs a notice to the agent bank.

exceptions.name: Availability short under the borrowing base
exceptions.description: The draw needed exceeds availability, so the treasurer defers some payments to the next conduit settlement or asks the lenders for a temporary increase.

exceptions.name: Conduit settlement day
exceptions.description: A conduit pays for a pool; the analyst checks the settlement statement, repays the bank line and funds the reserve account.

exceptions.name: Rejected payment
exceptions.description: The bank rejects a credit for an invalid account; funding re-verifies the vendor's banking by call-back and treasury releases the payment again, often the next day.

exceptions.name: Large wire or treasurer absent
exceptions.description: A wire above the treasurer's limit, or the treasurer's absence, needs the chief financial officer's approval, which can delay the release past the same-day cut-off.

exceptions.name: Afternoon payment run
exceptions.description: Payables approved after the morning cut-off, including held items cleared by funding, go through the check, position update, approval and release a second time.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from prior-day bank reports being available to the day's payments released and treasury entries posted
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a single-entity Canadian lessor releasing payments through a major bank portal

evidence.note: Derived, not observed: reports available about 6:30 a.m., payments released before the 2:15 p.m. ET same-day cut-off and entries posted late afternoon gives about 11 hours; a rejected payment, a late approval or a next-day advance pushes the day's work into the next morning.

benchmarks.unit: hours per year per treasury team
benchmarks.population: More than 100 large US and European companies (Kyriba survey, 2018)

evidence.note: Large multinational teams; a single-entity lessor needs far less.

benchmarks.population: AFP Payments Fraud and Control Survey respondents (mainly US)
One major Canadian bank's CAD payables service

pain_points.description: The cash position is rebuilt each morning by downloading bank reports into spreadsheets and re-keying collections, payables and forecasts, so it takes most of the analyst's morning and depends on one person's workbook.

evidence.note: Daily cash position is the largest spreadsheet task in Kyriba's survey.

pain_points.description: Approvals queue behind the treasurer's availability; when the treasurer is in meetings or away, payments miss the same-day cut-off and dealers wait another day for their money.

evidence.note: Typical of a small team with one primary approver; waits are author estimates.

pain_points.description: Payables approved after the morning release need a second run, which repeats the checks and the approval.

evidence.note: Author estimate of how funding approvals arrive through the day.

pain_points.description: Vendor banking changes requested by email are the main fraud exposure; treasury's duplicate and banking checks repeat part of the funding team's controls.

evidence.note: 62% of organisations hit by payments fraud in 2020 named business email compromise as the source.

pain_points.description: Collections on conduit pools must be tracked daily and remitted on schedule while the company services the contracts, which adds a manual reconciliation between cash application, the data warehouse and each facility's rules.

evidence.note: Rating criteria require daily monitoring where commingling is allowed.

sources.title: Keeping the lights on: the why and how of liquidity management
sources.supports: Setting the daily cash position in four steps: gather balances from bank portals and the ERP, forecast near-term inflows and outflows, identify surpluses and shortfalls (a shortfall can be met by drawing on a revolving credit facility), and execute transfers, investments or draws before settlement cut-offs, since late transactions may not settle until the next business day.

sources.title: Top 5 tasks of a treasury analyst
sources.supports: Treasury analyst tasks: reconcile bank activity to the ledger and resolve discrepancies with the bank, set the cash position daily and identify where to draw liquidity in a deficit, review bank fees, and use fraud prevention tools such as two-factor authentication on payment systems.

sources.title: Cut-off times for submitting payments (ScotiaConnect help)
sources.supports: Three daily cut-offs for Canadian dollar payables (5:00 a.m., 2:15 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. ET); a file sent by 2:15 p.m. reaches direct-clearing institutions by 6:30 p.m. the same day, indirect clearers up to two business days later; CAD wires within the Americas are due by 5:00 p.m. ET on the value date.

sources.title: What are security rights? (Web Business Banking help)
sources.supports: Business banking users hold separate rights to authorize EFT and wire payments created or last modified by other users and to authorize their own payments, so a company can require a second person to approve every payment.

sources.title: PaymentStream AFT guide for file upload
sources.supports: An uploaded AFT file from a user who requires approval waits as a pending task until another user with approver rights approves or rejects it; files must reach the processor before set delivery deadlines; originators review the daily returns, recalls and rejects report and correct rejected credit transactions. Read from the text copy saved under scratch by earlier work.

sources.title: Credit agreement dated as of December 15, 2005 (exhibit 10.12), Canadian dollar revolving and bankers' acceptance facility
sources.publisher: Jacobs Engineering Group Inc., filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.supports: Sample Canadian facility terms: a Canadian prime rate loan notice must reach the agent by 9:00 a.m. one business day before the borrowing date, in minimum amounts of Cdn$100,000; a bankers' acceptance drawdown, conversion or rollover notice is due by 9:00 a.m. three business days before, in minimum aggregate amounts of Cdn$1,000,000.

sources.title: DBRS clarifies commingling policy for structured finance transactions with revolving periods
sources.supports: When a servicer may no longer commingle, collections must reach a trust account at most within three business days of collection; partial commingling is allowed only with a daily asset test, daily monitoring for amortization events and a monthly officer certification.

sources.title: Treasury teams wasting almost 5,000 hours per year on spreadsheets
sources.supports: Kyriba survey of more than 100 US and European companies: treasury teams spend about 4,812 hours a year on spreadsheet work, the largest share (1,296 hours) on the daily cash position and 960 hours on payment and fund transfers.

sources.title: AFP survey: payments fraud increase attributed to coronavirus pandemic (2021 Payments Fraud and Control Survey)
sources.supports: In 2020, 74% of organisations were targets of payments fraud; 62% of those named business email compromise as the source and 76% were targeted by business email compromise attempts; cheques (66%) and wires (39%) were the payment types most affected.

sources.title: Building the cash muscle: how private equity is elevating the 13-week forecast
sources.supports: Private equity owners expect close cash visibility; in the example cash was reviewed weekly in the first year of ownership, with weekly actuals pulled from bank data and sorted into categories for variance analysis against the forecast.

sources.title: Wages: Financial analyst in Canada (NOC 11101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages for financial analysts: low $28.21, median $43.27, high $72.36 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one business day. Hands-on minutes are one day's work; the analyst's own steps follow each other with little wait, while the treasurer's approvals, the bank acknowledgement and the end-of-day posting carry the waits. The simulator adds every minute in sequence, so its median of about 0.7 days runs above the 0.45-day estimate: in practice the analyst drafts entries, answers funding queries and updates the forecast while waiting for approvals, and the afternoon run overlaps the morning's follow-up.

About 64 vendor payments and 20 broker commissions a business day follow from the organisation file's 1,400 fundings a month and the 32% broker channel; most go in one EFT file with wires for large or urgent items.

Treasury releases payments that the funding team has already approved with a second signature (audit-and-fund-contracts workflow); treasury's checks for duplicates and banking changes are a further independent control, not a re-audit.

Sample notice periods (9:00 a.m. one business day before a prime rate loan, three business days before a bankers' acceptance) come from a published Canadian facility of another borrower; this lessor's facility terms are not public. Most draws are planned a day ahead, so the agent bank step adds little wait to the day.
About half of business days have a bank line draw, repayment or bankers' acceptance rollover; the line is repaid from the three monthly conduit settlements. These frequencies are author estimates.

Conduit collections are tracked daily and remitted on each facility's schedule; the remittance itself is a transfer to the conduit's collection account and the monthly servicer report is a separate process (report-to-securitisation-funders). The process map lists no output from this process to the conduits, so none is added.

The borrowing base certificate from report-credit-facility-covenants is used as a standing input to check availability; the organisation file's process map does not list it, so it appears only under interfaces.inputs.
Weekly supplier payment runs and bi-weekly payroll funding appear only as forecast outflows and transfers; their approval belongs to pay-operating-suppliers and run-payroll-and-benefits.

The treasurer is the primary releaser and the chief financial officer the back-up; the chief financial officer is not in the process map's role list for this process but is the usual second signatory in a six-person treasury team.

Staffing: about 6 to 7 hands-on hours a day, mostly the analyst's, gives about 1.1 FTE at 130 productive hours a month, against 1.16 FTE stated; the organisation file's two treasury analysts leave about 0.8 FTE for covenant and borrowing base reporting and back-up.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
